crash.reportDamagePhrase.value: more than $1,000 in damage to one person’s property

notes.title: California’s adult phone rule
lines: An adult may not hold a phone or a wireless device while driving. Voice calls must be hands-free.
A mounted device may be operated only with a single swipe or tap — a long message, a search, a video, or repeated input is not allowed because the mount is legal.

notes.title: California’s other BAC lines
lines: A person under 21 also commits a separate offense at 0.05%.
A person on DUI probation may not drive with 0.01% or more.
Match the limit to the driver: adult per se 0.08%, under 21 zero tolerance at 0.01%, DUI probation 0.01%.

notes.title: The glove compartment counts
lines: In California an opened alcohol container may not be kept anywhere in the passenger compartment — the glove compartment included. Opened cannabis follows the same idea.
The trunk is the right place.

notes.title: California’s age and size rules
lines: A child under two rides rear-facing unless the child is at least 40 pounds or at least 40 inches tall.
A child under eight rides in a child restraint in the back seat; at 4 feet 9 inches a properly fitted seat belt is allowed.
A child at least eight but under sixteen must use an appropriate child restraint or the seat belt.

notes.title: Children alone, and smoking with a minor
lines: Do not leave a child six or younger alone in a car when the engine is running, the keys are inside, or another serious risk exists, unless someone at least 12 supervises.
Smoking a tobacco product in a vehicle with a minor present is prohibited, moving or parked — a fine of up to $100.

notes.title: Pickup beds in California
lines: People may not ride in the load area of a pickup or flatbed truck unless a legal restraint or another statutory exception applies.
An animal in a load space must be protected by an enclosure, side and tail racks at least 46 inches high, a cross-tether, or a secured container.

notes.title: Wipers on, lights on
lines: California also requires headlights whenever the windshield wipers are in continuous use because of weather — daytime included.

notes.title: California uses two separate clocks
lines: Injury or death: a written report to the CHP or local police within 24 hours, unless an officer at the scene has already made one.
Injury, death, or more than $1,000 in damage to one person’s property: a report to the DMV within 10 days, even if police or the other driver also report.
Do not swap the two: 24 hours is the police clock, 10 days is the DMV clock.

notes.title: The 30/60/15 minimums
lines: For policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025, California’s minimums are $30,000 for one person’s injury or death, $60,000 for two or more, and $15,000 for property damage.
A driver in a reportable crash who cannot show financial responsibility faces a DMV suspension.

notes.title: Lane splitting is legal in California
lines: California law defines lane splitting as a two-wheeled motorcycle traveling between rows of stopped or moving vehicles.
Do not block, chase, or deliberately narrow the space of a rider doing it lawfully. Check before opening a door or moving sideways, even in slow traffic.

notes.title: Move over — now for any vehicle with hazard lights
lines: Since 2026, California extends the move-over duty to any stopped vehicle displaying emergency, amber, hazard, or other warning lights — not only emergency vehicles.
The rule does not apply when a barrier separates the vehicle or it is not next to the highway.

notes.title: Red arrows and limit lines in California
lines: A red arrow means no turn at all until a green arrow or a green light appears — not even after a stop.
California calls the painted stop line a limit line. Exam questions use that name.

notes.title: Bicycle lanes before a right turn
lines: California lets you enter the bicycle lane within 200 feet of the corner to prepare a right turn.
Yield first to any cyclist already in the lane, then merge into it and turn from there.

notes.title: California’s 15 and 25 mph zones
lines: 15 mph at blind intersections, in alleys, and within 100 feet of a railroad crossing you cannot see for 400 feet in both directions.
Gates, a warning signal, or a flagman at the crossing lift that railroad limit.
25 mph near a school when children are outside or crossing, unless a lower limit is posted.

notes.title: Above 65, and when towing
lines: 70 mph applies only on highways where it has been approved and posted.
When towing a trailer or another vehicle, the maximum is 55 mph on any road.

notes.title: Double lines that form a barrier
lines: Two sets of double yellow lines spaced two feet or more apart form a barrier. Do not drive on or across it.
A two-way left-turn lane in the center may be used for no more than 200 feet before the turn.

notes.title: California curb colors
lines: California paints curbs in five colors, and the exam asks about them.
Each color has a different job:
bullets: Red: no stopping, standing, or parking, except at a marked bus zone.
Yellow: loading or unloading within the local time limit.
White: passengers or a marked mail area only.
Green: parking for a limited time.

notes.title: Steep roads in California
lines: On a steep, narrow road where neither vehicle can pass, California puts the duty on the driver facing downhill: yield and back up to the nearest safe place.

notes.title: Funeral processions
lines: A funeral procession led by a traffic officer has the right-of-way. Vehicles in it carry windshield markers or flags.
Never cut into or through a procession — interrupting one can bring a ticket.

notes.title: California’s parking distances at a glance
lines: Within 18 inches of the curb. At least 15 feet from a fire hydrant.
The exam likes to swap the two numbers; the smaller one belongs to the curb.

notes.title: Where California bans the U-turn
lines: Residence district: no U-turn when another vehicle is approaching within 200 feet from either direction, unless a signal controls that vehicle at the intersection.
Business district: only at an intersection or through a provided opening in a divided highway.
Never in front of a fire station, and never using its driveway to turn around.

notes.title: The five-vehicle turnout rule
lines: On a two-lane road where passing is unsafe, a slow vehicle followed by five or more vehicles must use a turnout or another safe area to let them pass.

notes.title: Exam trap: the number 200
lines: The number 200 appears in several California rules: center-lane travel, U-turn visibility, and bicycle-lane turn entry.
The exam may swap one for another. Read what the distance is measuring.

distraction-and-fatigue-q02.prompt: May an adult driver hold a phone for an ordinary call while driving?
distraction-and-fatigue-q02.explanation: Ordinary handheld phone use while driving is prohibited; calls must be hands-free.

distraction-and-fatigue-q03.prompt: Which interaction best fits the mounted-device exception?
choices: A single tap on a properly mounted device
distraction-and-fatigue-q03.explanation: The exception is limited to a single swipe or tap under the placement conditions.

seat-belts-child-safety-q04.prompt: Which fact can satisfy the rear-facing size exception for a child under two?
choices: At least 40 pounds or at least 40 inches
seat-belts-child-safety-q04.explanation: The exception uses 40 pounds or 40 inches.

seat-belts-child-safety-q05.prompt: Does the smoking-with-a-minor rule apply while the vehicle is parked?
seat-belts-child-safety-q05.explanation: The rule covers a motor vehicle moving or at rest when a minor is present.

equipment-loads-towing-q05.prompt: May a dog ride loose in an open pickup load space?
choices: Yes, if the tailgate is closed
No, use a compliant enclosure or restraint
equipment-loads-towing-q05.explanation: The animal must be protected from falling, jumping, or being thrown out.

crashes-and-insurance-q04.prompt: What is the police-report period after an injury or death collision?
crashes-and-insurance-q04.explanation: The written police report is due within 24 hours, unless an officer at the scene has made the report.

crashes-and-insurance-q06.prompt: After a reportable California collision, does a police report automatically replace the required DMV report?
choices: No, the DMV reporting duty can be separate
Only when both vehicles are insured
crashes-and-insurance-q06.explanation: The DMV report can be a separate duty from police and insurance reports.

bicycles-motorcycles-q05.prompt: Traffic is nearly stopped. Before changing lanes, what motorcycle risk remains?
choices: A lane-splitting motorcycle may be between rows
bicycles-motorcycles-q05.explanation: California recognizes lane splitting, so direct blind-spot observation remains important in slow traffic.

special-lanes-q03.prompt: What is the maximum distance you may travel in a two-way left-turn lane for the permitted maneuver?
special-lanes-q03.explanation: The maximum travel distance in a two-way left-turn lane is 200 feet.

road-markings-and-curbs-q04.prompt: Two sets of double yellow lines are separated by at least two feet. What do they form?
road-markings-and-curbs-q04.explanation: Two separated sets of double yellow lines form a barrier; never drive on or across it.

road-markings-and-curbs-q05.prompt: What does a red curb generally indicate?
road-markings-and-curbs-q05.explanation: Red generally prohibits stopping, standing, and parking, subject to the bus-zone exception.

uncontrolled-intersections-q06.prompt: Two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow California road where neither can pass. Which driver normally yields and backs up?
choices: The driver in the larger vehicle
uncontrolled-intersections-q06.explanation: California law generally places this duty on the descending driver when backing is necessary to pass safely.

choices: Yes, residential U-turns are always allowed
Yes, if you do not signal
No, the approaching vehicle is within 200 feet
u-turns-starting-backing-q01.explanation: In a residence district, an approaching vehicle within 200 feet makes the U-turn prohibited unless the signal-control exception applies.

u-turns-starting-backing-q04.prompt: You have a clear 200-foot view but are directly in front of a fire station. May you U-turn?
u-turns-starting-backing-q04.explanation: The fire-station prohibition remains even when visibility is adequate.
